screeningSummary: Man calls about his neighbor of fourteen years - since the ridge lights she has foil in three windows and won't come to barbecues
arcNotes: Comedy opinion arc with a heart - no sighting, all neighbor worry (Fake: the subject is Dot, not the sky). Vern reframes: the lights didn't scare her, they gave her a language. His advice: two chairs, one evening, no foil jokes

lines.text: Nobody asks her what - and you called the right line, just not for the reason you think. Twenty years of these calls taught me one thing: the lights didn't scare your neighbor. They gave her a language. People who watch the same ridge for forty years finally see something they can't explain, and some of them can't stop looking. The foil isn't fear of the sky - it's fear of being interrupted. You want Dot back? Don't ask about the foil. Take two chairs to that porch, sit down one evening, and ask her to show you what she looks at. Witnesses are lonelier than anyone knows, and Dot's had fourteen years of you not asking without laughing.
